en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Darkness by Night, 19.
The Training Rule on Cursing Others.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, some bhikkhunīs, not seeing their own belongings, said this to the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī:
"Venerable lady, would you please look for our belongings?
The bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī complained, grumbled, and became indignant.
“I must surely be the thief; I must surely be the shameless one, since when the noble ladies did not see their own belongings, they said this to me:
‘Noble lady, could you perhaps see our belongings?
Noble ladies, if I were to take your belongings, I would cease to be a monastic, I would fall away from the holy life, and I would be reborn in hell.”
“Furthermore, may she who has spoken thus to me with what is untrue cease to be a female ascetic, fall away from the holy life, and be reborn in hell!
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... were indignant, complained, and grumbled:
“How can the noble lady Caṇḍakāḷī curse both herself and another, as well as hell and the holy life?”... [as before]...

“Is it true, monks, that the nun Caṇḍakāḷī curses herself, others, hell, and even the holy life? “It is true, Blessed One. The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked her... [as before] ...and said: “Monks, this nun is foolish, unwise, and inexperienced. How can she curse herself, others, hell, and the holy life? This will not lead to the benefit of many people... [and so forth]. Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, from this day forward, nuns shall not curse themselves, others, hell, or the holy life. Whoever does so commits an offense of wrong-doing.”
"How indeed, monks, could the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī curse both herself and another with respect to hell and the holy life?

This, monks, does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence... And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule: ‘If a bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, should curse either herself or another, saying: “May you go to hell! May you live the holy life for the sake of hell!”—this is an offense of expiation.’”
“Whatever nun, however, should curse herself or another with reference to hell or the holy life, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Herself": [as before].
"Individual" means oneself.
"Another" means one who is fully ordained.
If she curses [a nun] with [the threat of] hell or [the loss of] the holy life, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
If she curses one who is fully ordained, perceiving her as fully ordained, with hell or the holy life, it is an offense entailing expiation.
If she curses one who is fully ordained, being in doubt [as to whether she is fully ordained], with hell or the holy life, it is an offense entailing expiation.
If one who is fully ordained, perceiving another as not fully ordained, curses them with reference to hell or the holy life, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she curses them with reference to the animal realm, the sphere of hungry ghosts, or human misfortune, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she curses one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If [the person] is not fully ordained, but she perceives her as fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If [the person] is not fully ordained, but she is doubtful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If [the person] is not fully ordained, and she perceives her as not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if it is for the sake of the welfare [of others],
or for the sake of the Dhamma.
[The exceptions are: one who has instruction as her primary concern,
one who is insane,
and one who is a first-time offender.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
